sources.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples
sources.locator: Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3, printed PDF pp. 15–22; the complete 47-page Chapter 1–2 PDF was retrieved and inspected for this range.
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the full official PDF temporarily to /tmp/bcs62-b28-owen-ch-intro.pdf and extracted its complete text to /tmp/bcs62-b28-owen-ch-intro.txt. Inspected all of printed pp. 15–22, including the sample-mean formulas, stated IID CLT and sample-variance consistency rationale, and the numerical-cancellation discussion and one-pass update in §2.3. Owen cites Chung for the CLT proof; this pair uses the fully proved live local Lindeberg–Lévy theorem instead.

contents.name: 2.1 Simple Monte Carlo estimate as an IID sample mean
contents.support: Defines the same sample-average target. The item states the library's IID and partial-sum conventions and makes the moment domains explicit.

contents.name: 2.1 Weak and strong laws for the Monte Carlo mean
contents.support: Supports weak and strong consistency. The local statements use the exact finite-first-absolute-moment hypotheses proved by the library's Khinchin and Kolmogorov IID laws.

contents.name: 2.1 Unbiasedness and variance sigma squared over n
contents.support: Supports the exact expectation and variance formulas, proved locally from expectation linearity and finite variance addition.

contents.name: 2.2 Bessel-corrected sample variance and plug-in standard error
contents.support: Supports the definition of s squared and s divided by square root n. The unbiasedness of s squared is not claimed here.

contents.name: 2.2 IID central limit theorem
contents.locator: §2.2, printed PDF p. 19, Theorem 2.1 and equation (2.11)
contents.support: Supports the positive-finite-variance IID limit statement. Owen cites Chung for the proof; the item applies the current fully proved local Lindeberg–Lévy theorem.

contents.name: 2.2 Consistency of the sample standard deviation
contents.locator: §2.2, printed PDF p. 19, paragraph following Theorem 2.1
contents.support: The source gives a weak-law argument for sample variance consistency. The local proof follows the planned stronger route, applying the IID strong law to Y and Y squared.

contents.name: 2.2 CLT-based and exact normal-theory confidence intervals
contents.reason: The approved design asks for the estimator, error moments, consistency, and the CLT; it does not claim interval coverage or finite-sample normal-theory inference.

contents.name: 2.2 Higher-order confidence-interval coverage accuracy
contents.reason: This source result has additional fourth-moment and nonlattice assumptions and concerns coverage error, neither of which is part of the approved BCS-25 scope.

contents.name: 2.3 Catastrophic cancellation in the second-moment variance formula
contents.locator: §2.3, printed PDF pp. 21–22, discussion of equation (2.17)
contents.reason: The numerical warning is retained in the A-page summary, but this pair proves statistical error claims and does not analyze floating-point roundoff.

contents.name: 2.3 Stable one-pass and paired-difference variance algorithms
contents.reason: The approved design defines and analyzes the standard error but does not specify computational update algorithms or prove their numerical stability.

sources.title: Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed.
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.2.1–2.2.3, printed pp. 56–58; Theorem 2.2.14, p. 65; Theorem 2.4.1, pp. 76–78; Chapter 3 Theorem 3.4.1, pp. 144–145. The complete 490-page PDF was retrieved and the complete named statements and proofs in these ranges were inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the full official fifth-edition PDF temporarily to /tmp/bcs62-b28-durrett-pte5.pdf and extracted its complete text to /tmp/bcs62-b28-durrett-pte5.txt. Read the finite-variance variance-addition and weak-law arguments, the integrable IID weak-law proof, the complete Etemadi strong-law proof, and the complete characteristic-function Lindeberg–Lévy proof. These treatments are independent of Owen and cross-check the local hypotheses and routes.

contents.name: Theorem 2.2.1: variance of an uncorrelated finite sum
contents.support: The live published corollary supplies the pairwise-independent finite-sum variance identity used locally.

contents.name: Lemma 2.2.2: L-p convergence implies convergence in probability
contents.reason: The local integrable IID weak-law supplier already states convergence in probability directly, so this auxiliary moment-to-probability lemma is not a premise of the page.

contents.name: Theorem 2.2.3: L-squared weak law
contents.support: The live published corollary gives the exact finite-variance IID mean-square and probability bounds.

contents.name: Theorem 2.2.14: weak law for integrable IID variables
contents.support: Supports weak consistency at finite first absolute moment; the local theorem also records the stronger L-one conclusion available from its supplier.

contents.name: Theorem 2.4.1: strong law for integrable IID variables
contents.support: Supports almost-sure consistency. The complete pairwise-independent Etemadi proof was inspected; the local statement uses the current proved IID L-one strong-law supplier.

contents.name: Theorem 3.4.1: IID Lindeberg–Lévy central limit theorem
contents.support: The full characteristic-function argument independently supports the limit statement; the local proof invokes the live fully proved theorem, including its explicit AC requirement.

contents.name: Theorems 3.4.2–3.4.4: complex near-one product approximation
contents.reason: These are intermediate lemmas in Durrett's alternative characteristic-function proof; the local Lindeberg–Lévy supplier has its own complete proof and different proved intermediate items.
